description:
In this compelling Bible Q&A, we explore deep and sometimes difficult questions about God’s justice, mercy, and divine timing. Why did Elijah kill the prophets of Baal? Can Satan ever be forgiven? Was Stephen’s stoning legal under Roman law? We also take a close look at topics like the timing of the biblical day, the second death, the seven last plagues, and the identity of false prophets. From Moses’ tablets to the lake of fire, from ancient executions to end-time events—this episode is filled with eye-opening, Bible-grounded insights for seekers of truth.


Send us your Bible Questions! 
By email: BibleQA@3abn.org 
By text: (618) 228-3975

QUESTIONS COVERED:

1.  For those persons killed by God in the first death, is the second death guaranteed for them or is there still hope?  

2.  Can you talk about "sunset to sunset" being the true day, as opposed to what the world thinks? I've always thought it's from Creation, but am I way off? Can you explain why a biblical day is from sunset to sunset instead of midnight to midnight?

3. What kind of tablet stone did Moses bring down from Mount Sinai? 

4. When did Jesus know he was God? At what age? Is it in the Bible? 

5. What does the Bible say about false prophets? 

6. When it came to the crucifixion of Christ, the Jewish high priest made claims that they nor any Jewish authorities, had no power to put any one to death. This is why they went to the Roman authority to have Christ sentenced to death. If this was the case, then why did the Jewish authorities stone Stephen to death without any outside interference from the Roman regime? Also, if the Jewish authorities had no power to sentence anyone to death, then why all of the fear of Saul?  If Jews couldn’t execute Jesus without Rome, how did they stone Stephen—and why fear Saul? 

7.  Is Satan here or locked up till later? 

8. In 1st King 18:40, why did Elijah slay the prophets of Baal after they surrendered? Commandment six says don’t kill. 

9. Revelation 20 tells us Satan and his followers were cast into the lake of fire forever.
With this in mind, what is Revelation 22:15 about? 

10.  With the world being so vast, why did God have his people take, fight, and kill to take over their lands. Why couldn't new land be cultivated? Why did God instruct his people to fight and kill over land?

11. Did God determine that Satan could never repent and be forgiven of his sins? If God is love, how is it possible that He ultimately plans to destroy Satan, a being created for good, in service to God? Can Satan be forgiven of his sins?

12. When will the seven last plagues take place?
